text: The following question stood in the name of Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant – 21 To ask the Minister for Defence (a) whether the Ministry can provide details on the safety audits and review processes that are regularly conducted by the SAF Inspector-General’s Office at training camps; (b) what are the common safety lapses that continue to occur during the SAF’s training and the reasons behind such occurrences and; (c) what steps have been put in place to ensure such lapses do not recur and the quality and standard of SAF’s training is not compromised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: From time to time, particular attention is paid to strengthen safety in specific areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: For example, the current area of focus is to reduce vehicular incidents, as the SAF operates a large number and range of vehicles, ranging from jeeps, utility vehicles and trucks, as well as armoured vehicles such as tanks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The SAF has been strengthening its training regime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Vehicle operators are trained progressively, first qualifying to drive, before gaining experience and confidence to operate larger and more complex vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Simulators and driving circuits are used to increase training hours and expand the range of training scenarios, including challenging and contingency situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: On our vehicular platforms, technologies such as vehicular proximity sensors and cameras have been adopted to reduce human judgement errors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Most recently, technologies like driver monitoring systems to detect driver fatigue, as well as sensors and video analytics to spot unsafe driving practices and safety transgressions have also been deployed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: Another area of attention is heat injuries, given our rising ambient temperatures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
text: The SAF has raised awareness of units, commanders and servicemen on the importance of heat acclimatisation and early identification of heat injury symptoms.
